title: 15th Annual Pershing Square Value Investing and Philanthropy Challenge
summary: The talk argues that PayPal is a high-quality compounder with a wide moat that has been unfairly punished, offering a significant buying opportunity with a specific price target for 2025. Conversely, the speaker views Carvana as a bankruptcy candidate due to high expenses and a desperate need to acquire a physical marketplace. The discussion also touches on Progeny's client base, noting that while Google and Meta are clients, the speaker does not express a specific investment view on those companies themselves.
thesis: The talk argues that PayPal is a high-quality compounder with a wide moat that has been unfairly punished, offering a significant buying opportunity with a specific price target for 2025. The discussion also touches on Progeny's client base, noting that while Google and Meta are clients, the speaker does not express a specific investment view on those companies themselves.

claims.claim: PayPal is gaining market share in the US e-commerce market, growing at 20% while the industry grows at 13.5%, and it remains the best option for conversion rates.
claims.quote: we don't have a concrete data point that says x percentage of customers of stripe actually transferred to paypal what we could provide is relatively paypal is still gaining market share because there's such a huge green field like e-commerce market within us is growing 13 and a half percent keger whereas paypal is growing 20 20 high teens percent kicker so paypal is taking market share

claims.claim: PayPal is untouchable in the world of small and medium-sized enterprises due to its ease of implementation and massive customer network of 400 million people.
claims.quote: um paypal is sort of untouchable in the world of small and medium-sized enterprises i think stripe is generally more catered towards up-and-coming tech companies like they were on airbnb for example and so i think very small merchants like paypal because it doesn't require very much coding to implement and then they also have this big network of customers that's sort of second to none with about 400 million people

claims.claim: PayPal is growing twice the rate of the US e-commerce industry, and its engagement program is working as transactions per account are up 19% annually.
claims.quote: in terms of how to think about the revenue growth going forward so within the e-commerce landscape so u.s e-commerce is growing 13 and a half percent of that growth say half of it goes to amazon of the rest of it paypal is has its eyes in terms of e-commerce growth when we think about the build-up to total revenue growth we had the different revenue drivers outlined where we do have a step down in terms of new customer account creation but the 390 millions that are currently on the platform that's global customers across 200 different regulatory markets so it's not just u.s demand but it's rather global demand that they're trying to expand into

claims.claim: PayPal's recent guidance cut provides flexibility to reset the base and improve messaging, and the stock is popping despite grim numbers because expectations were low.
claims.quote: so we don't see that as an impairment of the terminal value rather it provides paypal flexibility going forward to give better messaging and to reset the base one thing that i might highlight about it that maybe goes back to the question about our revenue growth excluding ebay which is rolling off transactions per account on an annualized basis we're up about 19 historically that growth rate has been closer to yeah we have it right there nine percent so that's an early sign that this engagement program is working which we were really pleased to see

claims.claim: The speaker views PayPal as a high-quality compounder with a deep moat that has been unfairly punished by the market, creating an attractive opportunity to buy.
claims.quote: we think that shifting customer acquisition increased engagement venmo modernization improving margins and capital return potential backstop a very attractive fundamental outlook for paypal for years to come the stock has been unfairly punished by the market which we think creates a very exciting opportunity to buy into a high quality compounder with a deep moat that's very durable
claims.speaker: mathesh marthaluru

claims.claim: The speaker expects PayPal to generate significant free cash flow and believes there is substantial capacity for share buybacks, potentially up to 90% of shares outstanding.
claims.quote: while we expect paypal to generate more than 50 billion dollars of free cash flow over the next five years with theoretical capacity to retire nearly 90 percent of all shares outstanding if they were to add some debt to the balance sheet
claims.speaker: mathesh marthaluru

claims.claim: The speaker sets a base case price target of $232 for year-end 2025, implying a 32% internal rate of return given the current stock price of $84.
